_doc: Seafood slug -> NOAA Fisheries commercial-landings species. The domestic (US wild-caught) pair for the seafood IMPORT streams already in the corpus, so a seafood ingredient can carry an import-vs-domestic-landings read the way crops carry import-vs-NASS-production reliance. Landings are US COMMERCIAL catch VALUE ($) + pounds (public domain, NOAA FOSS). This is a WILD-CATCH domestic figure paired against a largely-AQUACULTURE import stream — a chain seam the surface must NAME, never a clean apparent-consumption share.
_source: NOAA Fisheries FOSS (Fisheries One Stop Shop) commercial landings, collection=Commercial, 1950-present. Public domain (US Government work). Fetch runs on the operator's Mac -> data/noaa-landings.jsonl (rows: {year, ts_afs_name, tsn, state_name, region_name, dollars, pounds, collection}; dollars null where confidential).
_status: VERIFIED against the first real pull (40,029 rows, all 19 categories non-empty). Species strings + the specific-vs-rollup + wild-vs-farmed calls below were confirmed against the actual ts_afs_name values (e.g. SALMON, ATLANTIC = $0/null every year -> excluded; SOLE, DOVER = $3-5M vs $59M for all soles -> matched specifically).
_match_rules: categories[].match resolves a species set from data/noaa-landings.jsonl: rows whose ts_afs_name startsWith prefix, THEN restricted to `include` (exact names, a whitelist) if present, else minus `exclude` (exact names). National = sum across state_name by year (dollars-null rows excluded from the $ sum, kept for pounds). `**` names are NOAA aggregate/unclassified rollups — kept in the category total, labeled.

categories.label: Shrimp
categories.wild_note: US wild penaeid (Gulf/South Atlantic) + pandalid (cold-water); imports are mostly farmed — the wild-vs-farmed seam is wide here.

categories.label: Salmon (Pacific wild)
categories.wild_note: US wild = Pacific/Alaska (chinook, coho, sockeye, pink, chum). Atlantic salmon is farmed (US wild Atlantic landing is $0/confidential every year) and is EXCLUDED from the wild figure.

categories.label: Cod
categories.wild_note: Atlantic + Pacific cod, both wild; CODFISHES ** is the aggregate rollup.

categories.label: Haddock
categories.wild_note: US wild Atlantic haddock.

categories.label: Halibut
categories.wild_note: Pacific halibut dominates the value; Atlantic/California/Greenland roll up.

categories.label: Dover sole
categories.wild_note: US 'dover sole' = Pacific dover sole specifically — matched alone, NOT the whole 15-species sole group.

categories.label: Lobster
categories.wild_note: American (Maine) + spiny lobster roll up; both wild.

categories.label: Crab
categories.wild_note: Blue, dungeness, king, snow/tanner and more roll up; all wild.

categories.label: Scallop
categories.wild_note: Sea + bay scallop, wild-harvested.

categories.label: Clam
categories.wild_note: Wild clam landings; note some clams are also aquacultured (a seam on the domestic side too).

categories.label: Squid
categories.wild_note: Pacific (market) + Atlantic (Loligo/Illex) squid, wild.

categories.label: Octopus
categories.wild_note: US wild octopus landing is tiny (~$0.3M) — octopus on menus is overwhelmingly imported; degrades toward absence.

categories.label: Snapper
categories.wild_note: Red snapper + the wider Lutjanidae group roll up (the import code is broad too).

categories.label: Grouper
categories.wild_note: Black/gag/red and the wider Epinephelidae group roll up.

categories.label: Mahi-mahi (dolphinfish)
categories.wild_note: AFS common name is dolphinfish. US wild landing is small (~$2.7M) — mahi is largely imported; a wide seam.

categories.label: Tuna (all)
categories.wild_note: Yellowfin/bigeye/albacore/bluefin/skipjack roll up; a loin is a cut of the same landing.

categories.label: Ahi tuna (yellowfin + bigeye)
categories.wild_note: Ahi = yellowfin + bigeye specifically — matched as that pair, not the whole tuna group.

categories.label: Trout (wild)
categories.wild_note: US wild trout landing is tiny (~$0.1M, mostly lake trout). Menu trout is overwhelmingly farmed (NASS aquaculture) — degrades toward absence on the wild side.

categories.label: Anchovy
categories.wild_note: Pacific/northern anchovy, wild (reduction + bait fishery); small food landing.

categories.label: Sardine
categories.wild_note: Pacific sardine / pilchard, wild; landings swing with the stock's boom-bust cycle.

_deliberately_absent.tilapia: farmed + imported; negligible US wild landing (a domestic pair would come from NASS aquaculture, not NOAA).
_deliberately_absent.branzino: European sea bass; no US wild fishery.
_deliberately_absent.catfish: US catfish is farmed (NASS Catfish survey), not a NOAA wild landing.
_deliberately_absent.canned-tuna: a processed product, not a landing — the wild tuna catch is carried by tuna-loin / ahi-tuna.
